ORDER Appellants/claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173(1)of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing quantum part of impugned award dated 27/9/2014 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claim Case No. 88/2014; whereby, appellants/claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs.2,64,000/- alongwith interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition, for the death of one Preeti, daughter of appellants.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 26/12/2013 at about 2.45 pm due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. MP06AA2466, vehicle dashed the Preti due to which she succumbed to the injuries sustained by her and same gave rise to filing of claim petition by the appellant/parents before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act seeking total compensation of Rs. 31,25,000/-; however, by the impugned award learned Claims Tribunal awarded the compensation as mentioned hereinabove.
3. It is quantum part of the impugned award that claimants are before this Court assailing the impugned award.

According to learned counsel for the appellants the deceased was a brilliant student and used to give tuition to the student and thereby used to earn Rs. 3,000/- per month and therefore, looking to the principles of law, her income was liability to be assessed at Rs. 5,000/- per month, and therefore, learned Claims Tribunal erred in assessing his income at Rs.3000/- per month.

It is further submitted that Claims Tribunal also erred in applying the multiplier as per the age of parents whereas, as per the recent decisions of Apex Court, the multiplier should be applied as per the age of deceased.

It is further submitted that learned Claims Tribunal also erred in not awarding any amount towards future prospects, whereas, claimants were required to be awarded amount under the head future prospects to the extent of 40%.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No. 3 opposed the prayer and argued in support of impugned award.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

In the opinion of this Court, learned claims Tribunal did not err in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs. 3000/- per month in absence of any documentary evidence to the effect that he used to earn Rs. 5,000/- per month.

As regards multiplier, in the opinion of this Court, learned claims Tribunal erred in applying the multiplier as per the age of parents of deceased, whereas, in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Smt. Meenu Pawaia and Ors. Vs. Ashraf Ali and Ors., (Civil Appeal No. 6724/2021 decided on 18/11/2021), the multiplier as per the age of deceased would be applicable.

entities.text: Smt. Meenu Pawaia and Ors. Vs. Ashraf Ali and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 19 years at the time of accident, therefore, multiplier of 18 would be applicable.

At the same time, in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal did not err in deducting 1/2 towards personal expenditure, however, the appellants shall also be entitled to amount @ 40% towards future prospects.

7 . Thus, as per the above discussion, while assessing the income of deceased at Rs. 3,000/- per month her annual income comes to Rs. 36,000/-, 1/2 is required to be deducted towards personal expenditure and after deducting the same, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 18,000/- to which 40%
is required to be added towards future prospects in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., (2017)16SCC680, and after adding the same, the annual loss of dependency comes to Rs. 18,000 7,200 = 25,200/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., (2017)16SCC680,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Multiplier of 18 would be applicable and after applying the same, total loss of dependency comes to Rs. 25,200 x 18 = 4,53,600/- and claimants shall also be entitled to receive Rs. 50,000/- under conventional heads i.e. Rs. 15,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs. 15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs. 20,000/-
towards love and affection,
thus, total amount of compensation to which claimants are entitled for Smt.Laxmi Devi vs Surendra Singh on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105070783/

8 . The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs.2,64,000/-, therefore, the claimants shall be entitled to receive an enhanced compensation of Rs. 5,03,600 - 2,64,000 =
2,39,600/-.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. Appeal stands allowed in part with the modification in the impugned award to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
